package_info.package_versions: all published versions (auto-generated, no version specificity)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages are malicious because they are mass-produced with the intent to lure users to phishing and scam websites via links embedded in their README.md files. The packages lack any legitimate software functionality, serving solely as vehicles for social engineering attacks that drive traffic to phishing domains and eCommerce sites with referral IDs, potentially exposing users to credential theft and financial fraud.

execution_context.trigger: When the package is published and its README.md is viewed (either on npmjs.com, GitHub, or after local installation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When a user views the README.md file, the documentation displays a hyperlink to a shortened URL (tinybit.cc). If the user clicks the link, their browser is redirected through a chain of external sites, starting with a phishing or scam site (e.g., pdflivres[.]com), which may prompt for personal information or display invasive ads, and ultimately redirect to eCommerce sites with embedded referral parameters, resulting in potential credential theft and attacker profit.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The README.md contains a shortened URL that leads to a phishing or scam site, which is not expected in legitimate package documentation. The use of a URL shortener obscures the true destination, increasing the risk of user deception.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages use README.md to provide installation instructions, usage examples, and project information. They do not include links to unrelated external sites, especially via URL shorteners that conceal the final destination, nor do they attempt to drive traffic to phishing or scam domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate packages may link to official documentation or project websites, but they do not use obfuscated or shortened URLs to unrelated eBook downloads or third-party sites, nor do they mass-produce packages solely for this purpose.
key_indicators: README.md contains shortened URLs (e.g., tinybit.cc, bit.ly, etc.)
Links redirect to unrelated or suspicious domains (e.g., pdflivres[.]com)
No functional code present in the package—README.md is the only substantive file
Package metadata (name, description) appears auto-generated and unrelated to any real project

attack_chain.action: User discovers or is lured to the malicious NPM package and views the README.md file, either on npmjs.com, GitHub, or after installing the package locally.
attack_chain.leads_to: User sees a prominently placed phishing link in the README.

attack_chain.action: User clicks the shortened URL in the README.md, which initiates a redirect to a counterfeit eBook download site (e.g., pdflivres[.]com).
attack_chain.leads_to: User is prompted to download an eBook, solve a captcha, or provide personal information.

attack_chain.action: User is subjected to multiple redirects, captchas, and invasive advertisements, increasing engagement and exposure to further scams.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is eventually redirected to eCommerce sites with embedded referral IDs.

attack_chain.action: If the user makes a purchase on the eCommerce site, the attacker receives referral rewards. The user may also be phished for credentials or personal information during the process.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker profits from referral programs and may obtain sensitive user data.

behavioral_signatures: README.md files containing shortened URLs (e.g., tinybit.cc, bit.ly, goo.gl, etc.)
README.md links redirecting to unrelated or suspicious domains (e.g., pdflivres[.]com, scam eBook sites)
Packages with no functional code files (e.g., missing index.js, main entry point), only documentation with external links
Mass publication of similarly named packages with near-identical README content and auto-generated metadata
file_indicators: README.md with links to tinybit.cc or other URL shorteners
Packages lacking index.js, main.js, or any executable code files
Auto-generated or nonsensical package names and descriptions
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to tinybit.cc or other URL shortener domains
Redirect chains leading to pdflivres[.]com and other known phishing or scam domains
Final redirects to eCommerce sites with referral or affiliate parameters in the URL
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Automatically scan newly published NPM packages for README.md files containing shortened URLs or links to known phishing/scam domains. Flag packages that lack functional code or have auto-generated names and descriptions. Monitor for mass publication patterns from new or low-reputation publisher accounts. Track outbound traffic from documentation links to URL shorteners and known phishing domains. Correlate packages with similar README content and metadata to identify mass-produced scam campaigns.
